title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 334
paragraphs: And Menelaus, having come to Egypt and sailed up to Memphis, told the truth of these matters, and not only met with great entertainment but also received Helen unharmed, and all his own wealth besides. After he had been thus treated, however, Menelaus showed himself ungrateful to the Egyptians; for when he set out to sail away, contrary winds detained him, and since this condition lasted long, he devised an impious deed — he took two children of native Egyptians and made sacrifice of them. After this, when it became known that he had done so, he became abhorred, and being pursued he escaped and got away in his ships to Libya. But where he went after this the Egyptians were unable to tell. They said they had found out part of these things by inquiries, but the rest — namely what had happened in their own land — they told from sure and certain knowledge.
